subject: Capacity escrow request + provisional hold for VoyagerCloud
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity escrow request — VoyagerCloud (late-stage)

Team,

VoyagerCloud (late-stage opportunity, VGR-9812) is asking for a provisional capacity hold while procurement finishes contract redlines. Ask from Sales/AE: a short-term escrow so they can be guaranteed Dedicated slots by launch. High-level asks from the customer:
- Region: us-west-2 preferred, fallback us-east-1
- Start: target 2026-07-01
- Duration: initially 3 months (Q3), may convert to reserved capacity
- Capacity: estimate below (customer gave ballpark) — want 8 H100-equivalent instances, with peak concurrency approx 24 parallel sessions
- SLAs: standard Dedicated SLA; they may request an uplift if they convert to Reserved

Attached is the customer-supplied capacity worksheet (capacity_requirements.xlsx). Please run a short inventory check and tell me:
1) Can we provision an 8-slot H100-equivalent hold in us-west-2 for 2026-07-01 -> 2026-10-01?
2) If not exact H100s, what equivalent mix (A100+H100 fraction) would meet compute profile?
3) Any maintenance or already-committed holds in that window that conflict?
4) Recommended duration for escrow (we can propose 6 weeks hold-to-contract or full 3 months provisional).

Need answers by EOD Monday (2026-06-15) so Sales can align procurement timeline. If we can, we'll generate a provisional hold id and a short commit letter.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments: capacity_requirements.xlsx (customer worksheet)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity escrow request — VoyagerCloud (late-stage)

Sean — quick questions before I run the inventory:
1) Can you confirm whether the customer requires NVLink across the nodes (some of their models may prefer GB interconnect)?
2) Are they flexible on instance family? H100-80GB is ideal for the model mix they described, but we can accommodate an A100-80GB + H100 hybrid if they're ok with slightly different perf.
3) Do we want to tentatively reserve on physical hosts (hard hold) or soft capacity reservation (logical hold with preemption fallback)?

Current snapshot (short):
- us-west-2: 12 H100-equivalent slots free today, but 4 are already tentatively earmarked for a separate POC in late July (not yet committed).
- us-east-1: spare capacity but higher latency for customer.
- Maintenance window: some nodes have planned infra maintenance 2026-07-12 -> 2026-07-14 (ETA to avoid those).

I'll run an hourly availability check across zones and model-job history and come back with a binding answer and suggested hold type.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

[internal link: inventory snapshot noted]

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity escrow request — VoyagerCloud (late-stage)

Quick sizing notes after looking at the customer worksheet and historical workload profile:
- Suggested production footprint: 8 x H100-80GB-equivalent nodes (GPU vCPU/ram profile approximated from their batch/streaming ratio).
- Expected baseline utilization: 60% across the slot pool (spikey peaks). Peak concurrency ~24 sessions aligns with 3 sessions per node in peak — fits with 8 nodes.
- Cost/ops recommendation for escrow: suggest a 6-week provisional hold (escalate to 3 months only once procurement confirms because 3 months ties up capacity unnecessarily).
- If they insist on 3 months, recommend we put 2 nodes as true hard-reserved and keep the remaining 6 as soft-hold with automated fallback to region/variant.

Estimated impact on available pool (us-west-2):
- Current free-equivalent slots: 12
- After 8-slot hard hold: 4 remain for other opportunistic deals
- After suggested mixed hold (2 hard + 6 soft): effective hard-reduced capacity = 10 for other commitments if fallbacks triggered.

I'll attach a short calc (inline) — will follow up with a cleaned spreadsheet if you want the math in cells.

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Product Manager, Capacity & Performance
maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@voyagercloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Provisional capacity hold — next steps (VoyagerCloud)

Alice — thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, we can provision a provisional capacity hold while legal/procurement finish SOW/PO paperwork. Before we put a formal hold, can you confirm two quick items so we size the hold precisely:
1) Are you flexible on instance family (H100 preferred, but A100/H100 mix acceptable)?
2) Expected 95th percentile concurrency during peak (you mentioned ~24; is that steady or a short burst?)

Proposed workflow from our side:
- We place a provisional hold (non-billing) for up to 6 weeks while you finalize PO — if procurement needs the full 3 months we can extend provided a signed LOI/PO is in progress.
- Once hold is placed we'll send a short commit letter with HOLD id and the provisional dates.
- After contract signature, we'll convert the hold into a Reserved/Committed capacity product and finalize billing terms.

Attaching: Voyager SOW draft (voyager_sow_draft.pdf) for your legal team to review.

Let me know the two items above and procurement ETA and we'll proceed.

Best,
Sean

Attachments: voyager_sow_draft.pdf

From: Alice Park <alice@voyagercloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: VoyagerCloud Procurement <procurement@voyagercloud.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional capacity hold — next steps (VoyagerCloud)

Thanks, Sean. Confirming:
- We prefer H100 but can accept up to 50% A100 mix if needed.
- 95th percentile concurrency is closer to 18 sustained during business hours with spikes to 24 for short bursts (~5-10 minutes).
- Procurement ETA: signatures expected by 2026-07-02, PO to follow within 1 week after signature.

I've attached our procurement terms summary (voyager_po_terms.pdf). We'd like an anchor price to show to finance — can you provide a ballpark monthly committed price for the 8-node footprint (we'll finalize after SOW redlines)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alice
Alice Park
VP Product, VoyagerCloud
alice@voyagercloud.com

Attachments: voyager_po_terms.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity escrow request — VoyagerCloud (late-stage)

Team — final inventory check complete and hold placed. Summary: 
- Hold ID: HOLD-2026-1127
- Region: us-west-2 (primary), fallback us-east-1
- Provisioned footprint (provisional): 8 H100-equivalent slots (we'll accept up to 50% A100 as per customer)
- Dates: 2026-07-01T00:00:00-07:00 -> 2026-10-01T00:00:00-07:00 (3-month provisional window)
- Hold type: mixed (2 nodes hard-reserved, 6 nodes soft-reserved with automated fallback to us-east-1/A100 variants if needed)
- Impact: reduces hard-available pool in us-west-2 to 4 nodes during window; ops flagged maintenance window (2026-07-12 -> 2026-07-14) — hold excludes affected hardware.

Next steps for Sales/Procurement:
- Sean: send the short commit letter to Alice with HOLD id and provisional dates.
- I will create the internal record in the capacity ledger and add a ticket to convert hold -> reserved on signature (link: https://docs.internal.redwood/holds/HOLD-2026-1127).
- Dev: confirm if we should pre-assign physical hosts for the 2 hard nodes or keep them logical with dedicated isolation.

If nobody raises objections, I'll leave the hold live and mark calendar reminders 2 weeks before start and 1 week before the maintenance window.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity Orchestration
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
